parts.part_text: Production of new individuals from the vegetative part of parent is called ________.
parts.answer_text: Production of new individuals from the vegetative part of parent is called vegetative propagation.

parts.part_text: A flower may have either male or female reproductive parts. Such a flower is called _________.
parts.answer_text: A flower may have either male or female reproductive parts. Such a flower is called unisexual.

parts.part_text: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same or of another flower of the same kind is known as _________.
parts.answer_text: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same or of another flower of the same kind is known as pollination.

parts.part_text: The fusion of male and female gametes is termed as __________.

subject: science
question_text: Describe the different methods of asexual reproduction. Give examples.
answer_text:
The various modes of asexual reproduction in plants are as follows:
(i) Vegetative propagation: It is the ability of a plant to produce new plants from roots, stems, leaves, and buds. Vegetative propagation is divided into two types: Natural vegetative propagation and Artificial vegetative propagation.
(ii) Budding: It involves the formation of a new individual from a bulb-like projection called a bud. The bud grows and gets detached from the parent to form a new individual. It is commonly observed in yeast.
(iii) Fragmentation: It is a form of asexual reproduction where a new organism is formed from the fragments of the parent body. It is the only mode of asexual reproduction in Spirogyra.
(iv) Spore formation: Many non-flowering plants reproduce through spore formation. Spores are tiny cells protected by a thick wall. Fungi such as bread moulds reproduce asexually using this method.
final_answer: Thus, these are the various methods of asexual reproduction in plants.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of different methods and examples.

subject: science
question_text: Explain what you understand by sexual reproduction.
answer_text: Sexual reproduction is a process which involves production of seeds. It requires two parents. Most plants reproduce sexually with the help of flowers. The main function of a flower is to reproduce and therefore develop new seeds that can grow into new plants.
final_answer: Thus, sexual reproduction is essential for the production of seeds in plants.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the process and its significance.

subject: science
question_text: State the main difference between asexual and sexual reproduction.
answer_text:
Differences between sexual and asexual reproduction:
Asexual reproduction requires only one parent, while sexual reproduction requires two parents. In asexual reproduction, newly developed plants are identical to the parent and to each other, whereas in sexual reproduction, newly developed plants are not identical to parents. A flower is the reproductive part of a plant which contains the sexual organs of a plant, while special reproductive parts are not required for asexual reproduction. Examples of asexual reproduction include yeast, rose, jasmine, etc., while examples of sexual reproduction include flowering plants such as Hibiscus, potato, corn, papaya, etc.
final_answer: Thus, the main differences highlight the distinct processes of reproduction in plants.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding and comparison of two reproductive methods.

subject: science
question_text: Explain the difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination.
answer_text:
Differences between self-pollination and cross-pollination:
Self-pollination involves the transfer of pollen from the stamen to the pistil of the same flower, while cross-pollination involves the transfer of pollen from the stamen of one flower to the pistil of another flower of the same plant or that of a different plant of the same kind. Self-pollination occurs only in bisexual flowers, whereas cross-pollination occurs in both unisexual and bisexual flowers.
final_answer: Thus, these differences clarify the mechanisms of pollination in plants.

subject: science
question_text: How does the process of fertilisation take place in flowers?
answer_text: When pollen lands on stigma, it germinates and gives rise to a pollen tube that passes through the style and reaches the ovary of a pistil. When the pollen tube reaches an ovule, it releases the male gametes. A male gamete fuses with a female gamete in the ovule. This process is known as fertilisation. The cell which is formed after the fusion of a male and a female gamete is known as zygote. This zygote divides several times in order to form the embryo present inside the seed.
final_answer: Thus, fertilisation is a crucial step in the reproductive process of flowering plants.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the fertilisation process.

subject: science
question_text: Describe the various ways by which seeds are dispersed.
answer_text:
Seed dispersal occurs by the following agencies:
(a) Dispersal by animals - Birds and animals can eat the fruits and excrete the seeds away from the parent plant. Some seeds have barbs or other structures that get attached to the animal's body and are carried to new sites.
(b) Dispersal by wind - Seeds that get dispersed by wind are usually smaller in size or they have wings or hair-like structures.
(c) Dispersal by water - Many aquatic plants or plants that live near water have seeds that can float and are carried away by water.
(d) Dispersal by explosion - Sometimes the seeds are dispersed by the bursting of fruits with sudden jerks.
final_answer: Thus, these are the various ways by which seeds are dispersed.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of different seed dispersal methods.
